generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, owning your development means running one loop across every essay and report. You set a goal for the piece, judge your draft against the criteria for knowledge, communication and critical evaluation, and feed earlier feedback into the next submission. Across a module, those connected rounds are what raises a psychology student's work.
generatedProse.worked-example: Tom and Amara begin a psychology module with the same goal and the same early feedback: evaluate the studies, do not just describe them. Tom treats each essay as a fresh start, never checking his draft against the criteria or acting on that comment, and the same feedback returns. Amara sets a goal for each essay, reads her draft against the criteria, and carries one change forward each time. Over the module Amara's work improves, because for her the three strands ran as one practice.
generatedProse.summary: For a psychology student, owning your development is the three strands run as one loop: set a goal, judge the work against the criteria, and feed feedback forward into the next essay or report. You can now recognise that one practice and plan to keep it going. It is the repeated loop, not any single essay, that raises your work.

check.body: A student sets a goal for an essay, drives the work, judges the draft against the criteria, acts on earlier feedback, and the finished essay is stronger. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three strands work as one practice: directing, judging and feeding feedback forward together produced a stronger piece.
_items.feedback: Yes. The whole loop ran, and the work improved because of it.

_items.text: That the first essay was marked too generously.
_items.feedback: The point is not the mark. It is that the three strands together improved the work.

_items.text: That only students who already do well can use the three strands.
_items.feedback: The practice helped this student improve, whatever their starting point.

_items.text: That acting on feedback alone, without a goal or the criteria, is what improved the essay.
_items.feedback: Feedback was one strand. The gain came from running all three together.
